paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the trap Haman built for Mordecai is the one that caught him. Scripture says it plainly: "So they hanged Haman on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai." (Esther 7:10) Haman spent all that time and effort building something to destroy somebody else, and it ended up being the one thing that was waiting for him. Evil plans carry a price tag, and the one who made them is the one who ends up paying it.

Now look at Esther, because she matters just as much. She was the one who had to open her mouth and say, "grant me my life as my petition, and the lives of my people as my request." (Esther 7:3) I think that took everything she had. But she spoke up, and her people were saved because she did. When you know the right thing to say and the moment is finally in front of you, speak.

So what does this mean for you, baker? You don't have to fight your own battles by scheming, and you don't have to be scared of somebody else's scheme either. Do the right thing, speak the truth when it's your turn, and trust that it won't be wasted. And hold on tight, friend, because this story is NOT done.
